lead.zh-Hans: 脚印和轮子，在我的纸上各走各的。
lead.en: Footprints and wheels took separate lines on my paper.

text.zh-Hans: 在斯坦利公园的海堤步道，我沿着靠水的步行区域走，把内侧骑行区域也记在小图里。脚印用点，轮子用圈，画完却像两串不同的珠子。我想给两行添上名字，再寄给你看；先别拿它做项链，我还在画路。
text.en: On Stanley Park’s seawall, I followed the walking area nearer the water and noted the cycling area inside it. Dots for feet, circles for wheels: the sketch resembled two strings of beads. I want to label both lines before sending it home. Please postpone making a necklace; I am still drawing a path.
Talk about those paper beads
Label the dots and circles

lead.zh-Hans: 圆顶罩着植物，我用手罩住滚动的铅笔。
lead.en: The dome sheltered plants; my hand sheltered a rolling pencil.

text.zh-Hans: 看温哥华布洛代尔温室的圆顶，我在自己的本子上试画弯线，铅笔一松手就滚。赶紧按住，才没让它抢先离开。想到圆顶下面种着热带和亚热带植物，我给草稿写“各有各的屋顶”。我的那一份屋顶，暂时是一只手。
text.en: Looking at Bloedel Conservatory’s dome, I tried a curve in my notebook. The pencil rolled as soon as I released it. Under the real dome grow tropical and subtropical plants; under my hand, one pencil stayed put. “A roof for each of us,” I wrote beside the Vancouver sketch.
Describe the pencil’s temporary roof
Check whether the curve joins

lead.en: This menu drawing began at the surface.

text.zh-Hans: 在温哥华尝炙烧寿司，我想记下海鲜表面轻炙过的样子。菜单上涂色太用力，差点像整块焦了。我减淡铅笔，重新画一小格，再认真吃完。给你这份记录的是我那一口，不能让铅笔代替味觉下判断。
text.en: After trying aburi sushi in Vancouver, I sketched the lightly seared seafood surface. Heavy shading made my drawing look entirely burnt. I lightened the pencil and tried a smaller panel before finishing the meal. This records my serving; a pencil should not make taste judgments on my behalf.
Describe your own bite
Study the lightly shaded surface

lead.zh-Hans: 小方块有层次，我的图也想有。
lead.en: The little square had layers. My drawing wanted some too.

text.zh-Hans: 温哥华这块纳奈莫方块，我从侧面画，底层、甜馅和巧克力顶层分开记。第一遍画得像三本叠在一起的书。我给它添了盘子，才像一份点心。写信的时候还惦记那幅图，幸好我没有真给点心编页码。
text.en: For a Nanaimo bar in Vancouver, I drew the side: base, sweet filling and chocolate top. The first attempt resembled three stacked books. Adding a plate helped it become dessert. I was still thinking about the picture while writing home. Fortunately, I never actually numbered the pages of the snack.
Introduce the book-like dessert
Study the three layers from the side

lead.zh-Hans: 这一顿，铅笔先认了两次错。
lead.en: For this meal, the pencil admitted two mistakes.

text.zh-Hans: 和旅人聊温哥华的炙烧寿司与纳奈莫方块，我把画错的地方也讲了。太深的阴影、太像书的三层，听起来像铅笔自己出门吃饭。对方说菜单背面该留给这些。我写好了，正面认食物，翻过来就能认出写信给你的笨手。
text.en: Talking about Vancouver aburi sushi and a Nanaimo bar, I included my drawing mistakes: heavy shading and book-like layers. It sounded as though the pencil had dined without me. My listener suggested saving those details on the menu backs. The fronts show the food; the reverse reveals the awkward hand writing home.
Tell the story of the mistaken drawings
Read the notes on the reverse

lead.zh-Hans: 轻的一笔，分层的一笔，分开收好。
lead.en: A light stroke and layered lines went into separate sleeves.

text.zh-Hans: 整理温哥华菜单，我把寿司那张放亮处看，免得阴影画重；方块那张竖起来看，检查层线有没有连在一起。忙完把两张放平，自己也坐直。看纸有这么多姿势，吃饭倒只要好好坐着就够了。
text.en: Sorting my Vancouver menus, I held the sushi sketch to the light to check its shading, then raised the Nanaimo bar drawing to inspect the layer lines. Finally both went flat and I sat upright. Paper has required several viewing positions; eating merely required me to sit comfortably.
Describe the viewing positions
Check shading and layers separately

lead.zh-Hans: 收到“{reply}”，两串珠子有了名字。
lead.en: With “{reply},” the two strings of beads acquired names.

text.zh-Hans: 按你的回应，我在温哥华海堤小图旁写好“步行”和“骑行”，再折成长纸条。脚印的点和轮子的圈终于不会混着读。纸条只记自己看到的分区，不代替现场标识。给你翻看的时候，可以让手指散个很短的步。
text.en: Following your reply, I labeled the walking and cycling lines in my Vancouver seawall sketch and folded it into a long strip. Dots and circles now read differently. It records the separation I noticed, rather than replacing signs on the path. Your finger can take a very short walk along it at home.
Describe the two lines along the strip
Read the dots’ and circles’ labels

lead.zh-Hans: 海堤上来了一位口袋里的小骑手。
lead.en: A tiny cyclist needed help choosing a path.

text.zh-Hans: 一辆巴掌大的单车被举到我眼前，车座上还坐着小熊。孩子问它该走哪边。我认得温哥华斯坦利公园海堤的标识，这回走在靠水的步行区，没料到会碰见这么小的骑手。我说先让小熊下来歇歇，他便认真卸下小熊，塞进自己胸前的口袋，抱着车跟妈妈走了。口袋外还露着一对绒耳朵。
text.en: A child held up a palm-sized bicycle with a bear on the seat and asked which path it should take. I remembered the signs on Stanley Park’s seawall from being in Vancouver before. This time I was walking near the water, but I had not expected to advise such a tiny cyclist. I suggested that the bear get off for a rest. The child carefully unseated it, tucked it into his chest pocket, and carried the bicycle after his mother. Two furry ears stuck out above the pocket.

text.zh-Hans: 问问小骑手要不要歇脚
text.en: Ask whether the little cyclist needs a rest

text.zh-Hans: 看看口袋外的小熊耳朵
text.en: Look at the bear’s ears above the pocket
